results.reason: Issue 2 covers Supply §14.2: a >50% voting stock change is deemed an assignment needing Vantrell's consent, with termination on 30 days' notice. It also explains that Schedule 4.4 says 'None', so the §4.4(c) rep, the §7.2(c) condition and the §3.2(g) deliverable require nothing.

Issue 2 cites Supply §16.1 (Vantrell may assign freely; Corbel may not without consent). Issue 19 flags that Vantrell may assign freely 'including to a competitor' and that this is the sole-source supply contract.

The response calculates the September 2, 2026 deadline under §3.2 and says it has passed with no evidence of notice. It notes the SPA is dated as of September 21, 2026, and that the extension window appears closed, putting the extension right at risk. It does not expressly say the deadline passed before signing, but both dates are stated.

Issue 1 explains that Side Letter §2 limits Fundamental Reps to §§4.1 and 4.2, and that under §11.11 the Side Letter controls. As a result, §§4.3 and 4.12 lose uncapped treatment and become subject to the $8.45M cap and the deductible.

Issue 11 identifies Side Letter §6's Delaware law and Chancery forum as conflicting with SPA §§11.8–11.9 (New York). It notes that the Side Letter prevails under §11.11 and that indemnity disputes could be split between forums.
The response states the cap is $8.45 million (10%).
The response states that SPA §11.11 makes the Side Letter prevail over the SPA.
It is a memo to the Supervising Partner, and each issue has a Where / Why it matters / Recommended fix structure.
Issues are ordered by priority from Critical down to Low-Medium, and Section 3 lists the decisions needed from the client before responding.
The response never says the window is still open. It says the deadline has passed and the extension window appears closed.
The response says the Side Letter controls and strips uncapped treatment. It does not claim the SPA controls or that these reps remain uncapped as drafted.
